title: Variation and evolution
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for AQA GCSE Biology (8461) (status of the source: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms and clues: 4.6.2-c17 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; 4.6.2-c19 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; 4.6.2-c18 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; 4.6.2-c11 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition. Questions: 4.6.2-q08, 4.6.2-q10, 4.6.2-q14, 4.6.2-q09, 4.6.2-q11, 4.6.2-q15, 4.6.2-q12, 4.6.2-q13.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Tissue culture
items.clue: Growing identical new plants from small groups of cells.

items.label: Embryo transplants
items.clue: Cells from a developing animal are split apart and placed in host mothers.

items.label: Cuttings
items.clue: An old, simple way for gardeners to produce identical plants from a parent.

items.label: Inbreeding
items.clue: Mating closely related individuals, which can leave their offspring prone to disease or inherited defects.

questions.stem: A farmer chooses the cows that produce the most milk and breeds them together. From their offspring he again breeds those that produce the most milk, and he repeats this for many generations. Which statement about this process is correct?

options.text: It is natural selection, as the best cows survive and breed
It is genetic engineering, as the genome is being modified
It is selective breeding, as the farmer chose the parents
It was complete once the first chosen cows had been bred

questions.explanation: Selective breeding is the process by which humans breed animals for particular genetic characteristics, here the useful characteristic of producing more milk.

options.text: A gene is transferred to the cells of another organism
Parents with the desired characteristic are bred together
Cells from one organism are grown into identical copies
A faulty gene in a patient is replaced to cure a disorder

questions.explanation: Genes from the chromosomes of humans and other organisms can be 'cut out' and transferred to cells of other organisms, modifying the genome.

questions.stem: A nursery needs many new plants that are identical to one rare parent plant. Which statement is correct?

options.text: A gene from another plant would give identical copies
Tissue culture of the parent's cells gives identical plants
Cuttings from the parent give plants showing variation
One generation of breeding would give identical offspring

questions.explanation: Tissue culture uses small groups of cells from part of a plant to grow identical new plants, which is important for preserving rare plant species.

questions.stem: Which statement about selective breeding is correct?

options.text: It removes inherited defects from the breeds produced
It happens in wild populations with no human choice
It can lead to inbreeding in the breeds it produces
It adds a gene from another organism to the offspring

questions.explanation: Selective breeding can lead to 'inbreeding' where some breeds are particularly prone to disease or inherited defects.

questions.stem: Which statement about the uses of genetic engineering is correct?

options.text: Bacterial cells have been engineered to make human insulin
Tissue culture is used to insert genes in bacterial cells
Inherited disorders are now cured using genetic modification
Crops are engineered by breeding the best plants together

questions.explanation: Bacterial cells have been genetically engineered to produce useful substances such as human insulin to treat diabetes.

questions.stem: In adult cell cloning the nucleus is removed from an unfertilised egg cell, the nucleus from an adult skin cell is inserted, and an electric shock makes the egg cell divide to form an embryo. What are the embryo cells like?

options.text: They have the genetic information of the egg donor
They have genetic information varying from the adult
They have an extra gene added from another organism
They have the same genetic information as the skin cell

questions.explanation: These embryo cells contain the same genetic information as the adult skin cell whose nucleus was inserted into the egg cell.

questions.stem: Which statement about genetically modified (GM) crops is correct?

options.text: GM crops generally produce lower yields than other food crops
GM crops are grown from cells taken from one parent plant
GM crops may affect populations of wild flowers and insects
GM crops are used to cure inherited disorders in patients

questions.explanation: Concerns about GM crops include the effect on populations of wild flowers and insects, and some people feel the effects on human health have not been fully explored.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the main steps in the process of genetic engineering?

options.text: Enzymes isolate the gene, which a vector puts into cells
Enzymes cut out the gene and carry it into the cells
Cells are taken from an organism and grown into copies
The best parent organisms are bred to combine genes

questions.explanation: Enzymes are used to isolate the required gene, this gene is inserted into a vector, usually a bacterial plasmid or a virus, and the vector is used to insert the gene into the required cells at an early stage of their development.
